subject: Mutual Action Plan + Acceptance Tests: Synapse Therapeutics evaluation
messages:
From: Kate Morgan <kate@synapse.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: devon.hayes@synapse.com
Date: 2026-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluation timeline & acceptance criteria — can you share a concrete plan?

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Devon and I are aligned that we want a short, deterministic pilot: 4 weeks of evaluation, measurable acceptance tests, and a clear cutover path if we hit the targets. Can you send a mutual action plan / acceptance test checklist we can review with Security and Procurement?

High level asks from our side:
- Performance targets (p50/p95 latency for 256-token requests)
- Throughput for our expected steady load (~20 req/s) and burst behavior
- Data handling and retention guarantees for PII-sensitive prompts
- A simple pass/fail rubric so Procurement can greenlight a contract amendment quickly

We have an internal compliance review week of Oct 4 — would like the MAP before then so Security can pre-approve.

Best,
Kate Morgan
Director of Product Integrations
Synapse Therapeutics

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Kate Morgan <kate@synapse.com>, Devon Hayes <devon.hayes@synapse.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Evaluation timeline & acceptance criteria — can you share a concrete plan?

Kate / Devon —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a first-pass MAP (MAP-draft-v1.pdf) and a companion perf-test script. High-level summary below and then a short checklist you can hand to Security/Procurement.

Summary (4-week evaluation suggested):
Week 0 (kickoff): establish accounts, onboarding, security questionnaire exchange, and data redaction checklist.
Weeks 1–2 (functional + safety): integrate SDK routes, validate outputs on 100 representative prompts, run concordance checks against expected answers.
Week 3 (scale + perf): run throughput test to target 20 rps steady and 100 rps 30s bursts; measure p50/p95 for 256-token request.
Week 4 (acceptance & signoff): evidence collection, runbook handoff, and executive signoff.

Proposed acceptance gates (must all be met):
1) Latency: p50 <= 85ms, p95 <= 320ms for 256-token text-gen at 20 rps steady-state under our preconfigured batching.
2) Availability: >= 99.8% during test window (excluding scheduled maintenance).
3) Cost per 1k tokens does not exceed the agreed kitted rate in the PO for the pilot month.
4) Safety/ML: concordance >= 88% on your sampled evaluation prompts and no high-severity hallucination incidents on a 500-sample safety set.
5) Security: Redwood provides requested evidence (SOC 2 summary, data-retention policy, network diagram) and we complete redaction verification script (perf-test-script-01.txt).

Owners:
- Redwood technical owner: Monica Patel (cc) — runs perf and evidence collection.
- Redwood security contact: Karthik Iyer (cc) — handles artifact submission for Security.
- Synapse owners: Kate (Product) + Devon (Security).

Next steps:
- You review the attached MAP and tell us which acceptance gates you want as contract-level exit gates.
- If OK, we’ll provision a dedicated trial org and schedule a 45m kickoff next week.

Notes: attached files are stubs in this thread; final MAP will include links to test harness and the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kate Morgan <kate@synapse.com>, Devon Hayes <devon.hayes@synapse.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-24T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Evaluation timeline & acceptance criteria — details on acceptance tests

Kate / team —

Adding more detail on the acceptance tests so Security and Procurement have concrete artifacts. We referenced three types of tests in the MAP-draft; here's the runnable checklist we plan to use and what evidence we will produce.

1) Functional concordance suite (owner: Synapse / assisted by Redwood)
- 100 canonical prompts from Synapse mapped to expected intents/slots.
- Pass if >= 88% exact-intent match; we’ll provide a CSV of results and a short false-positive report.
- Evidence: concordance-results.csv (attached in final deliverable).

2) Safety regression sweep (owner: Redwood)
- 500-sample safety set (Synapse + Redwood combined) run through the pipeline.
- Flag any high/critical severity examples and provide remediation notes.
- Pass if no unresolved high-severity incidents after two business days.

3) Performance stress run (owner: Redwood ops)
- Tooling: our perf harness (script attached as perf-test-script-01.txt) will simulate 20 rps steady with 30s bursts to 100 rps.
- Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, error rate, tail-latency distribution.
- Pass criteria: p50 <= 85ms and p95 <= 320ms for 256-token requests, error rate < 1%.
- Evidence: perf-run-YYYYMMDD.log + Grafana dashboard snapshot.

4) Security artifact delivery (owner: Karthik / Redwood Sec)
- We will deliver SOC 2 summary, network diagram, data flow, and retention policy. Synapse Security will run a short redaction verification script against a synthetic dataset to confirm no PII retention.

Cutover/escape hatch: if any of the acceptance gates fail, we propose a single 7-day remediation window. If remediation does not close the gap, parties return to the PSC to decide whether to extend the pilot or terminate without penalty.

I’ll take the lead on running the perf window and compiling the evidence bundle. Jordan — if we can get Synapse signoff on these gates today/Friday, I’ll schedule provisioning for Monday.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Technical Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kate Morgan <kate@synapse.com>
Cc: Devon Hayes <devon.hayes@synapse.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Evaluation timeline & acceptance criteria — security notes and minor tweaks

Kate / team —

Two quick security/ops clarifications that will appear in the MAP final:
1) Key management: we will use customer-managed KMS for any pilot keys that need to persist beyond ephemeral testing. For the 4-week eval we typically use ephemeral keys but can switch to Synapse KMS if required — this will affect provisioning time by 24–48 hours.
2) Quantization/variance: some of the p95 tail behavior depends on chosen quantization/instance bootstrapping. Our recommended run for the pilot is int8-quantized model variant with continuous batching enabled. If Synapse requires a fp16 variant for fidelity reasons we should rebaseline latency targets (expect ~15–25% p50/p95 increase).

Also adding a minor wording change to the acceptance gates: replace “no high-severity hallucination incidents” with “no unresolved high-severity safety incidents within 48 hours of detection.” That gives a clear SLA for remediation.

I’ll attach the security evidence checklist (security-evidence-list.xlsx) in the final MAP.

Karthik Iyer
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kate Morgan <kate@synapse.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Hayes <devon.hayes@synapse.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Evaluation timeline & acceptance criteria — Synapse signoff to proceed

Jordan / Monica / Karthik —

This looks good and pragmatic. We reviewed the MAP-draft with Procurement and Security — Procurement wants the five acceptance gates (Latency, Availability, Cost, Concordance, Security remediation SLA) listed as contract-level exit gates; Security is comfortable with the evidence list and the 48-hour remediation SLA.

We signed the MAP in DocuSign and uploaded the signed copy (Synapse-signed-MAP-docusign.pdf) to the link below. Please provision the trial org and schedule kickoff for Monday, Oct 5 at 10am PT.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/sign/abc123-synapse-map
Internal ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SALESDOC-213

Thanks — excited to get started.

Kate Morgan
Director of Product Integrations
Synapse Therapeutics
